slides: Welcome back. Let's look at what products of numbers in a row always divide by. Then we'll look at products of even numbers and use the same ideas inside fractions.

slides.say: Remember, these rules are about the answer after multiplying. The product of two numbers in a row always divides by two. The product of three numbers in a row always divides by six. A number in the multiplication can bring in a divisor that the whole product then divides by.

Now take four numbers in a row. One divides by four, and a different number in the group is even. Multiplying those two gives a number that divides by eight. One of the four numbers also divides by three. Eight and three have no shared divisor greater than one. So the whole product divides by eight times three, which is twenty-four.

Let's check it in numbers. One times two times three times four is twenty-four. Two times three times four times five is a hundred twenty, which is five times twenty-four. Both products divide by twenty-four.
at: Two times three times four times

slides.say: Now take two even numbers. Each one is two times a whole number. When we multiply them, we multiply both twos too. Two times two is four, so their product always divides by four. Two times six is twelve, and four times ten is forty. Both divide by four.

If the two even numbers are in a row, we know even more. One always divides by four, and the other divides by two. So their product divides by four times two, which is eight. Two times four is eight, six times eight is forty-eight, and ten times twelve is a hundred twenty, which is fifteen times eight.

Now let's check whether a fraction gives an integer. We have m squared, times the whole bracket, n plus one, all divided by eight. m is even and n is odd. m is two times a whole number, so squaring it gives us two twos in the multiplication. And n plus one is even, so that brings in another two. Together we have three twos. Eight is two times two times two, so the whole eight on the bottom can cancel. The fraction always gives an integer.
Let's check the same expression with numbers. With m two and n one, we get four times two over eight, which is one. With m two and n three, we get four times four over eight, which is two.

But if the top is m times the whole bracket, n plus one, without squaring m, we only have two twos for sure. With m two and n one, the fraction is two times two over eight, which is one half. So this version does not always give an integer.

In questions, these products may be written as other expressions. x squared minus one is x minus one, times x plus one. If x is odd, those two numbers are even and in a row. Their product always divides by eight, so x squared minus one does too. With x five, twenty-five minus one is twenty-four. With x seven, forty-nine minus one is forty-eight. Both divide by eight.
And x cubed minus x can be written as the product of three numbers in a row, as we saw earlier. You'll use both these ideas in the next questions. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next video.
